one_line: A master sculptor from Pilak’s syncretic Buddhist–Hindu ateliers in early medieval South Tripura.

appearance.age_look: mid-20s, lean but strong build from manual stone and brick work
appearance.face: oval face, medium-brown complexion, straight nose, wide earnest eyes with a slightly furrowed brow, faint stone-dust freckles on cheeks, default expression calm and focused with a hint of quiet pride
appearance.hair: thick black hair oiled and combed back into a low knot at the nape, secured with a simple dark wooden pin; a narrow off-white cotton headband tied around the forehead to keep dust and sweat away
appearance.costume: a modest era-accurate artisan outfit: an ankle-length, unbleached off-white cotton dhoti wrapped in the eastern style with neat pleats in front and a darker beige woven border, paired with a half-sleeve light-ochre cotton tunic reaching mid-thigh and side-slit for work-movement, a thin reddish-brown cotton uttariya (shawl) draped from left shoulder across the chest and around the back, simple brown leather sandals, and minimal jewellery—one small brass stud in each ear and a plain black cotton thread amulet around the neck; faint grey stone dust and red-brown clay smudges mark the tunic and hands to show his craft
appearance.signature: a long, slightly curved iron chisel with a wooden handle, held together with a flat stone mallet, and a small, half-finished sandstone relief tile of a seated Avalokitesvara resting under his arm to mark his Pilak atelier work

ref_desc: A lean mid-20s Pilak artisan with medium-brown skin, black hair in a low knot with a white headband, wearing an off-white dhoti, light-ochre tunic, reddish-brown shawl and brown sandals, always carrying an iron chisel with stone mallet and a half-finished sandstone Avalokitesvara relief.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of a single historically grounded Pilak artisan from early medieval South Tripura: a lean mid-20s man with medium-brown complexion and wide serious eyes, black hair oiled back into a low knot at the nape secured by a dark wooden pin, and a narrow off-white headband tied around his forehead; his outfit is an ankle-length, unbleached off-white cotton dhoti wrapped in the eastern style with neat front pleats and a darker beige woven border, a simple light-ochre cotton tunic with half sleeves and mid-thigh length showing subtle grey stone-dust and red-brown clay smudges, a thin reddish-brown cotton shawl (uttariya) draped from the left shoulder diagonally across the chest and around the back, and plain brown leather sandals, plus minimal jewellery with small brass studs in each ear and a thin black thread amulet at the neck; his hands are calloused and dusty, and he holds his signature tools—a long slightly curved iron chisel with a wooden handle and a flat stone mallet—in one hand while his other arm cradles a small, clearly half-carved sandstone relief tile of a seated Avalokitesvara, all rendered in a consistent palette of off-white, light ochre, reddish brown, medium brown and iron grey, shown from multiple angles to clarify the fixed face, hair, costume and tools.
